messages:
Alex (Customer): Hey team — since ~09:10 UTC our app is seeing a bunch of high-latency requests and intermittent 502s. We expect traffic to go to eu-west but Cloud logs show responses from us-west. Also noticed a big jump in egress billing for that window.

Lina (Support): sorry about that — can you paste a sample request id/headers and roughly what times you saw it? I'll escalate to SRE once we have a sample.

Alex (Customer): sample req id: req_0a1b2c3d4e timestamp ~2026-03-17T09:12Z. Here's a curl I used: 

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```

Response headers we saw: `X-Served-Region: us-west`, `x-request-latency-ms: 420`. Body was a 502.

Lina (Support): thanks — tagging @Jordan (SRE) and noting ops-bot recorded healthcheck anomalies around that time.

ops-bot: [ALERT] 09:11:55 UTC healthcheck: probe ip=34.55.66.77 region_tag=eu-west check=ok ttl=20s origin_detected_geo=us-west -> recorded mismatch.

Jordan (SRE): thanks, looking. Quick hypothesis: probe IP (34.55.66.77) is NATing behind a provider IP that geoip resolves to us-west, causing our edge routing to send to us-west. That would explain served-region mismatch and cross-region egress.

Mira (Eng-Platform): +1. We've had a recent NAT rotation on the probe fleet and the CDN/geoip table may not have propagated to the routing layer for a small window. If the healthcheck source IP looks us-west to the router, routing policy could prefer us-west and the failover fallback might be sticky until probe updates.

Jordan (SRE): repro steps I'd like to run — can someone from DevOps run the probe from that IP and capture `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Region-Header` on the edge? Also check the routing decision log for that request id. Example quick test: 

```
# simulate probe from suspect IP via curl from bastion
curl -H "Host: api.redwood.example" \
  -H "X-Forwarded-For: 34.55.66.77" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Region: eu-west" \
  -v https://edge-eu.example/healthcheck
```

Look for lines like: `route_decision: region=us-west reason=geoip(src=34.55.66.77)` in the edge logs.

Lina (Support): I'm filing a billing note to figure cross-region bytes during 09:08-09:20 UTC. Customer wants a credit if confirmed.

Mira (Eng-Platform): short-term mitigation: we can push a routing override for the customer route to prefer eu-west while we clear geoip caches. Command: `redwoodctl routes update --customer <cust-id> --region-preference eu-west --sticky-duration 300` (doing manually requires a rollback plan). Also bump healthcheck TTL to 60s so transient NAT rotation doesn't flip the sticky failover quickly.

Jordan (SRE): I'll take the routing override and TTL change, and add a quick audit to detect probe-origin-ip != probe-declared-region. Applying now and watching.

ops-bot: [ACTION] routes:update started by Jordan (SRE) at 09:18:12 UTC: set region_preference=eu-west for route cust-123, sticky_duration=300s. healthcheck_ttl updated 20->60s for probe-group-prod.

Jordan (SRE): applied. I also added a temporary log line to flag future mismatches: `healthcheck_geo_mismatch{probe_ip="34.55.66.77", declared_region="eu-west", detected_region="us-west"}` — will alert if >3 per 10m.

Alex (Customer): after the override latency dropped to ~55ms and the 502s stopped. Thanks. Please keep me posted on credits for the extra egress.

Lina (Support): noted, I'm prepping a credit request for the 12-min window. Jordan/Mira — please add a short RCA note when you have the root cause.

Mira (Eng-Platform): root cause draft: probe NAT rotation produced source IP that geoip DB classified as us-west. Routing logic uses geoip of source IP for region selection; healthcheck declared region mismatch led to sticky fallback to us-west until route override. Fixes: 1) ensure probe control plane updates origin mapping to use SNI-based region token (in progress), 2) add geoip drift metric and alert, 3) make routing fallback respect `X-Redwood-Region` header for healthchecks.

Jordan (SRE): follow-ups — I'll add the alert to incidents playbook and schedule a small change to prefer declared-region for healthchecks only. Also will run a quick scan of probe fleet for other IPs with mismatched geoip.

Lina (Support): customer credited for cross-region egress for 09:08–09:20 UTC, will confirm in email. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Alex (Customer): appreciate the quick turnaround. Will monitor and ping if anything else shows up.
